summary: The article provides a generally accurate explanation of the Repo Rate and its impact, but contains incorrect information regarding the specific dates and rate of the August 2026 MPC meeting.

claims.claim: The Reserve Bank of India's Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) just finished its latest bi-monthly meeting from August 6-8, 2026.
claims.note: Multiple sources indicate the RBI MPC meeting in August 2026 was held from August 3-5, 2026, with the decision announced on August 5, 2026.

claims.claim: the MPC announced on August 8, 2026, that it would keep the benchmark Repo Rate unchanged at 6.50%.
claims.note: The RBI MPC announced on August 5, 2026, that the Repo Rate would remain unchanged at 5.25%.

claims.claim: The Repo Rate is the interest rate at which commercial banks borrow money from the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) for short periods.
claims.note: The Repo Rate is indeed the rate at which the RBI lends short-term funds to commercial banks.

claims.claim: The six-member Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) of the Reserve Bank of India decides the Repo Rate. It includes three members from the RBI and three external members appointed by the government.
claims.note: The MPC consists of six members: three from the RBI and three external members nominated by the Government of India.

claims.claim: The MPC meets bi-monthly, meaning every two months, to review the economic situation and make decisions on the Repo Rate and other monetary policy instruments.
claims.note: The MPC meetings are held at least four times a year (specifically, at least once a quarter), and it publishes its decisions after each such meeting.

claims.claim: The Repo Rate is the interest rate at which commercial banks borrow money from the RBI. The Reverse Repo Rate is the interest rate at which the RBI borrows money from commercial banks.
claims.note: This distinction between Repo Rate and Reverse Repo Rate is consistently explained across various sources.

article_title: What is the Repo Rate and Why Did the RBI Just Keep It Unchanged?
